title: fix(app-shell): the AI chat object read rides the authenticated fetch, and the fetch ratchet follows a fetch alias
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuDJAbBe3iTrFcF7GZrucZ32)_

Fixes #37242

## What changes

- **N4 — the AI chat page's object read.** `appOfObject` (which app a record hand-off from the chat opens under) moves out of `AiChatPage.tsx` into `app-shell/src/console/ai/appOfObject.ts` and reads `/api/v1/meta/object/<name>` through `createAuthenticatedFetch()`, keeping `credentials: 'include'`. `AiChatPage.tsx` imports it; its three call sites are unchanged. The `AiChatPage.tsx` row leaves the shrink-only allow-list of `sameServerFetch.bearer.ratchet.test.ts` (its reason, an open PR on the file, no longer held).
- **N1 — the ratchet sees through a fetch alias.** `bareCookieOnlyCalls` now also counts a call through a local name bound to the global `fetch`:
  - `const f = fetch` (or `window.` / `globalThis.` / `self.fetch`) counts in every scanned tree;
  - a name bound to a `?? fetch` / `|| fetch` fallback (`const doFetch = opts.fetchImpl ?? fetch`) counts in app-shell and the console only.

## A decision made here

The fallback form is **not** followed in the renderer packages. There `const doFetch = apiFetch ?? fetch` is the documented channel (the ratchet's own header: the host's `apiFetch`, falling back to the global `fetch` only in a host that mounts none), and following it everywhere flags 17 conforming sites (`ShareDialog`, `ObjectChart`, `MePermissionsProvider`, `queueClaim`, `useRowApprovalLocks`, …). App-shell and the console build `createAuthenticatedFetch` per call, so there a `?? fetch` name is the bare fetch under another name. The header says so, and the detector's case table pins both sides (a renderer-tree `apiFetch ?? fetch` name reads 0, a plain alias reads 1).

## Why

`#37185` moved the shell's same-server calls onto the authenticated fetch and added the ratchet. Its L1 left two follow-ups: the ratchet did not see `flowDraftChecks.ts`'s `doFetch` alias, so reverting that conversion stayed green; and the chat page's object read was still cookie-only, so under a bearer-only session every record hand-off from the chat fell back to the Setup shell.

## Verification

- Ablations against this head (each restored after):
  - `flowDraftChecks.ts:104` back to `opts.fetchImpl ?? fetch` — on `main` the ratchet stays 4/4 green; here it goes red, naming `flowDraftChecks.ts:114 :: doFetch(…)`.
  - `appOfObject.ts` back to the bare `fetch` — red, naming `appOfObject.ts:19 :: fetch(…)` (no row allows it).
- New `console/ai/__tests__/appOfObject.bearerSession-37242.test.ts`, against a server that answers only the bearer: with a token stored the read carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>` beside `credentials: 'include'` and returns the owning app; CONTROL, no token: the read goes out cookie-only and falls back to `setup`.
- `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run` over `packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/`, `packages/app-shell/src/preview/` and the ratchet: 780 tests green; the ratchet re-run on this head (rebased on `main` bdbe01e05): 4/4.
- `type-check` for `@object-ui/app-shell`: clean. `eslint` on the changed files: 0 errors.
- `overlap-check`: exit 0.
